concepts.name: Nature of light
concepts.oneLineSummary: Light is electromagnetic radiation that is transverse and travels at 3e8 m/s.

concepts.name: Monochromatic and polychromatic light
concepts.oneLineSummary: Monochromatic light has single wavelength; polychromatic has multiple wavelengths.

concepts.name: Ray and beam of light
concepts.oneLineSummary: A ray is the straight-line path of light; a beam is a bundle of rays.

concepts.name: Types of beams
concepts.oneLineSummary: Beams may be convergent, divergent or parallel.

concepts.name: Transparent translucent opaque
concepts.oneLineSummary: Objects classified by how much light they transmit.

concepts.name: Rectilinear propagation
concepts.oneLineSummary: In a homogeneous medium light travels in straight lines.

concepts.name: Reflection of light
concepts.oneLineSummary: Bouncing back of light from a surface separating two media.

concepts.name: Plane mirror
concepts.oneLineSummary: Highly polished smooth surface that forms virtual erect images.

concepts.name: Image characteristics of plane mirror
concepts.oneLineSummary: Virtual, erect, same size, laterally inverted, equal distance.

concepts.name: Number of images by two mirrors
concepts.oneLineSummary: n = 360/θ - 1 when 360/θ is even; special rules when odd.

concepts.name: Deviation by plane mirror
concepts.oneLineSummary: Deviation δ = 180° - 2i for a single reflection.

concepts.name: Deviation by two mirrors
concepts.oneLineSummary: Total deviation by two mirrors inclined at θ is 360° - 2θ.

concepts.name: Lateral inversion
concepts.oneLineSummary: Left-right interchange in the image formed by a plane mirror.

concepts.name: Laws of reflection
concepts.oneLineSummary: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection; rays and normal coplanar.

concepts.name: Spherical mirrors
concepts.oneLineSummary: Concave and convex mirrors; focus, centre of curvature, mirror formula.

concepts.name: Refraction at plane surface
concepts.oneLineSummary: Bending of light when it enters a different medium; Snell's law.

concepts.name: Total internal reflection
concepts.oneLineSummary: Complete reflection when light travels from denser to rarer medium above critical angle.

qna.question: Define optics and state the nature of light according to the notes.
qna.answer: Optics is the branch of physics that deals with the study of light. Light is an electromagnetic radiation that is transverse in nature and travels with a speed of 3 × 10⁸ m/s. After analysis it was proposed that light possesses a dual nature comprising both ray optics (geometric optics) and wave optics (physical optics).

qna.question: Distinguish between monochromatic and non-monochromatic light.
qna.answer: Monochromatic light is a wave of light that has a single colour or a single wavelength; examples are a laser beam and the light from a sodium vapour lamp. Non-monochromatic or polychromatic light consists of various colours or multiple wavelengths; sunlight is a common example.

qna.question: What is a ray of light and a beam of light?
qna.answer: A ray of light is the straight-line path along which light travels, representing the direction of propagation of energy from a source. A beam is a bunch or bundle of light rays. Beams are classified as convergent, divergent or parallel according to the behaviour of the rays that constitute them.

qna.question: Describe the three types of beams of light.
qna.answer: A convergent beam is one in which the diameter of the beam gradually decreases and the rays meet at a point. A divergent beam is one in which the rays appear to meet at a point when produced backwards and the diameter increases as the rays proceed forward. A parallel beam consists of rays that remain parallel to one another so that the diameter of the beam stays constant.

qna.question: Classify objects according to their interaction with light.
qna.answer: Objects are classified as transparent, translucent or opaque. Transparent objects allow light to pass through them, translucent objects allow partial transmission, and opaque objects do not allow light to pass through them. The classification determines how shadows and images are formed.

qna.question: What is meant by an isotropic medium for light?
qna.answer: An isotropic medium is one in which the optical properties of light are the same in all directions. In such a medium light travels with the same speed irrespective of the direction of propagation, which simplifies the application of the laws of reflection and refraction.

qna.question: Explain shadow formation on the basis of the rectilinear propagation of light.
qna.answer: In a homogeneous medium light travels along straight paths. Consequently an opaque object placed between a point source of light and a screen casts a shadow with a sharply defined boundary. The sharp boundary is a direct consequence of the rectilinear propagation of light rays.

qna.question: Define reflection of light.
qna.answer: Reflection of light is the phenomenon in which a beam of light incident on the boundary separating two media is bounced back into the first medium from the surface on which it strikes. The boundary is called the interface and the reflected light obeys the laws of reflection.

qna.question: What is a plane mirror?
qna.answer: A plane mirror is a highly polished smooth surface that reflects light regularly. The interface is the boundary line separating the mirror and the surrounding medium. Incident rays falling on the mirror give rise to reflected rays that form images of objects.

qna.question: Define the terms incident ray, reflected ray and angle of deviation.
qna.answer: The incident ray is the line that originates from the object and falls on the plane mirror. The reflected ray is the line that bounces back from the mirror after the light strikes it. The angle of deviation is the angle between the imaginary continuation of the original path of the incident ray and the actual reflected ray.

qna.question: Describe the characteristics of the image formed by a plane mirror.
qna.answer: The image formed by a plane mirror is virtual, erect, of the same size as the object, and exhibits lateral inversion (left appears as right). The distance of the image from the mirror is equal to the distance of the object from the mirror. These properties hold for a single plane reflecting surface.

qna.question: How many images are formed by two plane mirrors inclined at an angle θ?
qna.answer: When two plane mirrors are inclined at an angle θ the number of images is given by n = 360°/θ − 1 if 360°/θ is even, and by n = 360°/θ − 1 (for symmetric placement) or n = 360°/θ (for unsymmetric placement) if 360°/θ is odd. If 360°/θ is a fraction the number of images equals the integer part of that fraction.

qna.question: Calculate the number of images formed by two mirrors inclined at 90°.
qna.answer: For θ = 90°, 360°/θ = 4, which is even. Therefore n = 4 − 1 = 3. Three images are formed when an object is placed between two mirrors at right angles to each other.

qna.question: Calculate the number of images formed by two mirrors inclined at 45°.
qna.answer: For θ = 45°, 360°/θ = 8, which is even. Therefore n = 8 − 1 = 7. Seven images are observed when the mirrors form a 45° angle.

qna.question: Calculate the number of images formed by two mirrors inclined at 60°.
qna.answer: For θ = 60°, 360°/θ = 6, which is even. Therefore n = 6 − 1 = 5. Five images are formed by mirrors inclined at 60°.

qna.question: What is the formula for the deviation produced by a single plane mirror?
qna.answer: If the angle of incidence is i, the angle of reflection is also i. The deviation δ is the angle between the original direction of the incident ray and the reflected ray, given by δ = 180° − 2i. This expression follows directly from the geometry of the incident and reflected rays.

qna.question: Explain the deviation produced by two plane mirrors inclined at an angle θ.
qna.answer: When a ray is reflected successively from two mirrors inclined at angle θ, the total deviation suffered by the ray is 360° − 2θ. The intermediate angles can be expressed as δ₁ = 90° − i and δ₂ = 2θ, and their sum yields a constant total deviation independent of the angle of incidence.

qna.question: What is the difference between a real object and a virtual object for a plane mirror?
qna.answer: A real object is one from which rays are actually diverging toward the mirror. A virtual object is one toward which rays are converging (as if they would meet behind the mirror). The image of a real object by a plane mirror is virtual, while the image of a virtual object can be real.

qna.question: List the phenomena studied under ray optics and under wave optics.
qna.answer: Ray optics (geometric optics) deals with reflection, refraction, double refraction and total internal reflection. Wave optics (physical optics) deals with the wave nature of light, interference, diffraction, polarisation and the Doppler effect. The two approaches complement each other in describing the behaviour of light.

qna.question: What are luminous and non-luminous sources of light?
qna.answer: Luminous sources produce light on their own; the Sun is a primary example. Non-luminous sources do not produce light themselves but can be seen by reflected light; a black body or any ordinary object illuminated by another source is non-luminous.

qna.question: How is the number of images determined when 360°/θ is a fraction?
qna.answer: When 360°/θ is not an integer the number of images is taken to be the integer part of that quotient. For example, if 360°/θ equals 17.38 the number of images is 17. This rule avoids fractional images that have no physical meaning.

qna.question: What is lateral inversion and how does it appear in a plane-mirror image?
qna.answer: Lateral inversion is the interchange of left and right sides in the image relative to the object. A plane mirror produces an image that is laterally inverted: the right hand of the object appears as the left hand of the image and vice versa. The inversion occurs only in the left-right sense, not up-down.

qna.question: Why does a plane-mirror image appear to be as far behind the mirror as the object is in front?
qna.answer: By the law of reflection the paths of the reflected rays, when extended backwards, meet at a point that is the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front. This geometric equality of object and image distances is a direct consequence of equal angles of incidence and reflection.

qna.question: State the condition under which the number of images is 360°/θ − 1 for an odd value of 360°/θ.
qna.answer: When 360°/θ is an odd integer and the object is placed symmetrically with respect to the two mirrors, the number of images is 360°/θ − 1. If the object is placed unsymmetrically the number becomes simply 360°/θ. The distinction arises from the coincidence or non-coincidence of certain image positions.

qna.question: What is meant by the dual nature of light?
qna.answer: The dual nature means that light exhibits both particle-like behaviour (ray optics, photoelectric effect) and wave-like behaviour (interference, diffraction, polarisation). Ray optics treats light as travelling in straight lines, while wave optics treats it as oscillatory disturbances. Both descriptions are needed for a complete understanding.

qna.question: How does the angle of deviation depend on the angle of incidence for a plane mirror?
qna.answer: The deviation δ = 180° − 2i decreases as the angle of incidence i increases. When i = 0° (normal incidence) the deviation is 180° (the ray reverses direction). When i approaches 90° the deviation approaches 0°, corresponding to grazing incidence with almost no change in direction.

qna.question: What is the interface in the context of reflection?
qna.answer: The interface is the boundary line that separates the reflecting surface (mirror) from the surrounding medium. All angles of incidence and reflection are measured with respect to the normal drawn at the point of incidence on this interface.

qna.question: Why does an opaque object cast a sharp shadow when illuminated by a point source?
qna.answer: Because light travels in straight lines in a homogeneous medium, the region behind the opaque object is completely deprived of rays from the point source. The boundary between the illuminated and dark regions is therefore geometrically sharp, producing a well-defined shadow.

qna.question: Calculate the number of images for two mirrors inclined at 22°.
qna.answer: 360°/22° ≈ 16.36. Since the value is not an integer the number of images is taken as the integer part, which is 16. The notes list this result as an illustration of the fractional rule.

qna.question: Calculate the number of images for two mirrors inclined at 75°.
qna.answer: 360°/75° = 4.8. The integer part is 4, so four images are formed. The notes record this value as an example of the rule applied to a non-integer quotient.

qna.question: What is the total deviation when a ray is reflected from two mutually perpendicular mirrors?
qna.answer: When two mirrors are at right angles (θ = 90°) the total deviation is 360° − 2 × 90° = 180°. The ray emerges travelling in a direction opposite to the original direction after the two successive reflections.

qna.question: How are the intermediate deviations δ₁ and δ₂ related for two mirrors?
qna.answer: From the geometry of successive reflections one finds δ₁ = 90° − i and δ₂ = 2θ. Their sum is independent of the angle of incidence and equals 180° − 2θ when the mirrors are inclined at θ, confirming the overall constant deviation.

qna.question: Why is the image formed by a plane mirror said to be virtual?
qna.answer: The reflected rays diverge after leaving the mirror. When these diverging rays are extended backwards they appear to meet at a point behind the mirror. Because the rays do not actually converge there, the image is virtual and cannot be obtained on a screen placed at that location.

qna.question: What is the significance of the dual classification of light into ray optics and wave optics?
qna.answer: Ray optics successfully explains the formation of images by mirrors and lenses using the concept of rays travelling in straight lines. Wave optics is required to explain interference, diffraction and polarisation, which cannot be understood on the basis of rays alone. Together they provide a complete description of optical phenomena.

qna.question: How does the size of the image compare with the size of the object for a plane mirror?
qna.answer: The image formed by a plane mirror is of the same size as the object. This equality of size, together with the equality of object and image distances, follows from the geometry of reflection and the fact that the mirror is plane.

qna.question: State the rule for the number of images when the object is placed unsymmetrically between two mirrors.
qna.answer: If 360°/θ is an odd integer and the object is placed unsymmetrically, the number of images is simply n = 360°/θ. The extra image that would coincide in the symmetric case does not coincide, resulting in one additional distinct image.

qna.question: Summarise the key geometric properties of reflection from a plane mirror.
qna.answer: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane. The image is virtual, erect, laterally inverted, of the same size as the object, and located as far behind the mirror as the object is in front. The deviation produced by a single reflection is 180° − 2i.
